chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Umar ibn Udhayna, from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), 'May God keep you well! For each salat, is the beginning of the time superior, or its middle, or its end?' So he said: 'Its beginning. Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, loves from the goodness what is hastened.'

key_terms.أوّل الوقت: The beginning of the prayer time — the most virtuous time to perform salat
key_terms.يُعَجَّل: That which is hastened — doing good deeds at the earliest opportunity

ai.seo_question: What is the best time to pray salat according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Zurara asked Imam al-Baqir (AS) whether the beginning, middle, or end of each prayer's time is most virtuous. The Imam declared that the beginning is best, citing a prophetic hadith that God loves good deeds done promptly. This established an important Shia jurisprudential principle that praying at the first available time is preferred, rooted in divine love for swiftness in obedience.
word_analysis: may He set you right / may God keep you well

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Zurara who said,

‘I said to Abu Ja’farasws, ‘May Allahazwj Keep youasws well! For each Salāt, is the beginning time superior, or its middle, or its last?’ So heasws said: ‘Its beginning. Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Loves from the goodness what is hastened with’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ’Udhaynah from Zurarah who has said the following:

“I once said to abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, of the timing for Salah (prayer), what portion is better? Is it the beginning, the middle or the end of time?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is the beginning of it; the Messenger of Allah has said, “Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, loves of good things the most that which is done earlier.’”
